title: Boxes, Fibonacci, notes
goal: Use rectangles, Fibonacci and notes, and learn the measure tool.

objectives.text: Draw a rectangle on flat candles.
Draw Fibonacci from a low to a high.
Leave a note on a candle.

slides.text: A rectangle is a box you draw on the chart. It marks a zone of time and price. A flat run of candles fits in a box.
slides.title: The rectangle

demo.caption: Real Apple prices. The candles stay in a tight zone.

slides.text: Fibonacci levels are lines between a low and a high. They mark set shares of the move, like 38%, 50% and 62%.
slides.title: Fibonacci levels

slides.text: Click the low first. Then click the high that came after it. The lines fill in between.
slides.title: Drawing Fibonacci

demo.caption: Real Apple prices. The price climbed, then slipped back.

slides.text: Some traders watch these lines. They are a guess, not a rule. Prices often ignore them.
slides.title: Not a law

slides.text: The Text tool lets you write a note on a candle. A note says why you looked.
slides.title: Notes

slides.text: The measure tool shows how far the price moved between two points. It shows dollars. It shows percent too.
slides.title: The measure tool

questions.prompt: What is a rectangle used for?

options.text: Marking a zone on the chart

questions.explanation: A rectangle marks a zone of time and price.

questions.prompt: Fibonacci levels sit between a low and a high.
questions.explanation: Click a low, then a high. Lines fill the gap.

questions.prompt: Prices must stop at a Fibonacci level.
questions.explanation: No. Fib lines are a guess. Prices often ignore them.

questions.prompt: What is a note on a candle for?
questions.explanation: A note is for you. It says what you saw.

questions.prompt: What does the measure tool show?
questions.explanation: It shows how far the price went.

questions.prompt: Draw a rectangle on candles 8 to 15. That is the flat part.
questions.explanation: The box covers the flat part. Its top meets the high. Its bottom meets the low.

questions.prompt: Draw a Fib. Start at the low of candle 3. End at the high of candle 22.
questions.explanation: Candle 3 is the low spot. Candle 22 is the top of the climb. Lines fill the gap.

questions.prompt: Find the top price. Write a note on it.
questions.explanation: The tall spike is candle 13. A note helps you find it.

questions.prompt: Use the measure tool. Start at the close of candle 5. End at the close of candle 23.
questions.explanation: The measure tool joins two closes. It shows how far the price rose.
